rules.title: Limits on considering criminal history and blanket bans in tenant screening
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not consider arrests that did not lead to conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile justice matters, and may not impose blanket bans on all people with a criminal history.
rules.coverage_text: Housing providers covered by FEHA (landlords, property managers, tenant screening companies and others) screening rental applicants.
rules.citation: Cal. Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA) as described in CRD Housing FAQ, https://calcivilrights.ca.gov/housing/
rules.quoted_span: Housing providers cannot consider some types of criminal history including arrests that did not lead to a conviction, records that are sealed or expunged, or records or matters processed in the juvenile justice system. Housing providers are also prohibited from having “blanket bans” of all people with a criminal history.
rules.ambiguity_note: Summary FAQ page; does not cite the specific statute or effective date.

rules.title: Denial based on criminal conviction must be directly related to tenancy
rules.requirement: A housing provider denying an application based on a criminal conviction must show the conviction is directly related to the applicant's ability to be a good tenant and not a threat to health and safety of others or property, considering the nature and severity of the crime and time elapsed.
rules.coverage_text: Housing providers covered by FEHA screening rental applicants.
rules.citation: Cal. Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA) as described in CRD Housing FAQ, https://calcivilrights.ca.gov/housing/
rules.quoted_span: If a housing provider intends to deny someone’s application based on a criminal conviction, it must be directly-related to someone’s ability to be a good tenant and to not be a threat to the health and safety of others and the property.
rules.ambiguity_note: Summary FAQ page; no statute cited.

rules.title: Source of income discrimination prohibited (including Section 8 vouchers)
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not refuse to rent or apply different terms based on a tenant's source of income, including Section 8 vouchers, and must comply with paperwork requirements of rental assistance programs. Advertising such as 'No Section 8' is also prohibited.
rules.citation: Cal. Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA) as described in CRD Housing FAQ, https://calcivilrights.ca.gov/housing/
rules.quoted_span: No. California law protects tenants from discrimination based on how a tenant will be paying rent (“source of income”).
rules.ambiguity_note: Summary FAQ page; no statute cited.

rules.title: No pet deposits or pet rent for service animals and emotional support animals
rules.requirement: Tenants cannot be charged pet deposits or pet rent for service animals or emotional-support animals.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants with service animals or emotional-support animals as a disability accommodation.
rules.citation: Cal. Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA) as described in CRD Housing FAQ, https://calcivilrights.ca.gov/housing/
rules.quoted_span: Service animals and emotional-support animals are not subject to breed, size, or weight restrictions ordinarily applied to pets, and tenants cannot be charged pet deposits or pet rent for them.
rules.ambiguity_note: Summary FAQ page; no statute cited.
